title: H0709 (2021 Regular): Domestic Violence

other_topics: judicial-criminal-justice: Section 1 (new s. 784.04875, F.S.) — creates a first-degree misdemeanor for any act of domestic or dating violence, a crime that is not about guns

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Florida); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Florida text (Introduced, 2021-02-03; official copy, https://www.flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2021/709/BillText/Filed/PDF (LegiScan doc 2272127))
provenance.note: Introduced text (filed 2021-02-03); no passage vote. Section 2 (s. 790.065) adds a cross-reference to the new disability to the dealer sale prohibition; not quoted. Subsections (1)-(2) of s. 790.233 are renumbered.

operative_text:
Section 3 (s. 790.233, F.S.), subsection (3): A person may not have in his or her care, custody, possession, or control a firearm or any ammunition if the person: (a) Has been issued a final injunction that is currently in force and effect, restraining that person from committing acts of domestic violence, as issued under s. 741.30, or from committing acts of stalking or cyberstalking, as issued under s. 784.0485; or (b) Has been convicted of a misdemeanor offense of domestic violence.
Section 3 (s. 790.233, F.S.), subsection (4): A person convicted of a misdemeanor offense of domestic violence must, upon conviction, be required to surrender all firearms and ammunition in his or her possession as provided for in subsection (5).
Section 3 (s. 790.233, F.S.), paragraph (5)(a): Upon convicting a defendant of a misdemeanor offense of domestic violence under this section, the court shall order the defendant to surrender to the local law enforcement agency all firearms and ammunition owned by the defendant which are in the defendant's custody, control, or possession, except as provided in subsection (6), and to surrender any license to carry a concealed weapon or firearm issued under s. 790.06.
Section 3 (s. 790.233, F.S.), subsection (7): A person who violates this section commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.
Section 4 (new s. 790.234, F.S.), subsection (2): When at the scene of an alleged act of domestic violence, a law enforcement officer must remove a firearm from the scene if: (a) The law enforcement officer has probable cause to believe that an act of domestic violence has occurred; and (b) The firearm is in plain view or is discovered during a consensual or other lawful search.
